title: Inheritance, Polymorphism, and Prototypes
summary: Extend classes with extends and super, override methods for polymorphism, see the prototype chain underneath, and build custom error classes.
intro: Many things in a program are special versions of something more general: a truck is a vehicle, a circle is a shape. Inheritance lets a class reuse another class and change only what differs. Here you extend classes, override methods so one loop handles many kinds, peek at the prototypes underneath, and write your own error types.

steps.title: extends and super

example.title: Pets and dogs
example.prompt: Read lines like `dog Rex collie` or `animal Tom`, build a Dog or a plain Animal, and print each description.
example.stdin:
dog Rex collie
animal Tom
dog Bella poodle
example.output:
Rex is an animal. Breed: collie
Tom is an animal.
Bella is an animal. Breed: poodle
example.explanation: `Dog` calls `super(name)`, so `Animal`'s constructor sets `this.name`, then `Dog` adds `breed`. `Dog`'s `describe()` starts with `super.describe()`, which returns the animal sentence, and appends the breed. For `animal Tom` the third word is missing, `breed` is `undefined`, and the ternary builds a plain `Animal` that never reads it.

practice.title: Trucks and vehicles
practice.prompt:
Read lines like `truck Volvo 18` or `vehicle Fiat` and print a description of each vehicle.

1. Write `class Truck extends Vehicle` whose constructor takes `make` and `capacity`, calls `super(make)`, stores `capacity`, and sets `this.wheels` to 6.
2. Override `describe()` in `Truck` to return `super.describe()`, a space, then `Capacity: <capacity> tons`.
3. For each line, build a `Truck` (capacity converted with `Number`) when the first word is `truck`, otherwise a `Vehicle`.
4. Print each description in input order.

Input:

```text
truck Volvo 18
vehicle Fiat
truck Scania 25
```

Expected output:

```text
Volvo has 6 wheels. Capacity: 18 tons
Fiat has 4 wheels.
Scania has 6 wheels. Capacity: 25 tons
```

tests.stdin:
truck Volvo 18
vehicle Fiat
truck Scania 25
tests.output:
Volvo has 6 wheels. Capacity: 18 tons
Fiat has 4 wheels.
Scania has 6 wheels. Capacity: 25 tons

Mini has 4 wheels.
Kia has 4 wheels.

hints: Set `this.wheels = 6` after `super(make)`, which sets it to 4 first.
Start from `super.describe()` and add the capacity in one template literal.

steps.title: Overriding and polymorphism

example.title: Shape areas
example.prompt: Read one shape per line, build it with `parseShape`, and print each area, the total, and a few `instanceof` checks.
example.output:
circle: 12.57
square: 9.00
triangle: 10.00
Total: 31.57
All shapes: true
Circles: 1
Shape area: not implemented
example.explanation: `parseShape` returns a different class for each first word. The loop calls `describe()`, which lives on `Shape`, and `describe()` calls `this.area()`, which runs the override on the real object. Every shape passes `instanceof Shape`, but only one passes `instanceof Circle`. A bare `Shape` has no real area, so its `area()` throws and the catch prints the message the program wrote.

practice.title: Monthly payroll
practice.prompt:
Read one employee per line and print each monthly pay, the total, and a few `instanceof` checks.

1. Write `Salaried`, `Hourly`, and `Intern`, each extending `Employee`. Override `monthlyPay()`: `salary / 12`, `rate * hours * 4`, and a flat `1000`.
2. Finish `parseEmployee(line)` with a `switch` on the first word: `salaried <name> <salary>`, `hourly <name> <rate> <hours>`, or `intern <name>`.
3. Print `<name>: <pay>` for each employee in input order, then `Total: <sum>`, both to 2 decimal places.
4. Print `All employees: <true or false>` (every item is an `Employee`) and `Interns: <count>` (items that are an `Intern`).
5. Call `monthlyPay()` on `new Employee("Temp")` inside try and print `Employee pay: <error message>`.

Input:

```text
salaried Ana 52000
hourly Bo 20 35
intern Cy
```

Expected output:

```text
Ana: 4333.33
Bo: 2800.00
Cy: 1000.00
Total: 8133.33
All employees: true
Interns: 1
Employee pay: not implemented
```

steps.title: Prototypes under the hood

example.title: Where properties live
example.prompt: Read property names and report the prototype links of a Dog, then label each name as own, inherited, or missing on `rex`.
example.output:
typeof Dog: function
rex -> Dog.prototype: true
Dog.prototype -> Animal.prototype: true
shared fetch: true
name: own
breed: own
describe: inherited
toString: inherited
bark: missing
example.explanation: `name` and `breed` are set on `rex` itself, so `Object.hasOwn` says own. `describe` is on `Animal.prototype` and `toString` on `Object.prototype`: not own, but `in` finds them on the chain, so they are inherited. Nothing has `bark`. `rex.fetch === max.fetch` is true because both read the single function stored on `Dog.prototype`.

practice.title: Truck properties
practice.prompt:
Read property names, report the prototype links of a Truck, and label each name for `volvo`.

1. Print `typeof Truck: <result>`.
2. Print `volvo -> Truck.prototype: <true or false>` and `Truck.prototype -> Vehicle.prototype: <true or false>` using `Object.getPrototypeOf`.
3. Print `shared describe: <true or false>`, comparing `volvo.describe` with `scania.describe`.
4. For each name in input order, print `<name>: own` if it is an own property of `volvo`, `<name>: inherited` if it is found elsewhere on the chain, or `<name>: missing`.

Input:

```text
make capacity describe toString fly
```

Expected output:

```text
typeof Truck: function
volvo -> Truck.prototype: true
Truck.prototype -> Vehicle.prototype: true
shared describe: true
make: own
capacity: own
describe: inherited
toString: inherited
fly: missing
```

tests.output:
typeof Truck: function
volvo -> Truck.prototype: true
Truck.prototype -> Vehicle.prototype: true
shared describe: true
make: own
capacity: own
describe: inherited
toString: inherited
fly: missing

typeof Truck: function
volvo -> Truck.prototype: true
Truck.prototype -> Vehicle.prototype: true
shared describe: true
wheels: own
constructor: inherited

hints: Check `Object.hasOwn(volvo, key)` first, then `key in volvo`.
`wheels` is own even though `Vehicle` sets it: the constructor writes it onto the instance.

steps.title: Custom error classes

example.title: Validate users
example.prompt: Read lines of `name age`, with `-` for a missing name, and print `ok` for valid users or which field failed.
example.output:
ok: Ada (36)
ValidationError on name: required
ValidationError on age: must be 0-150
ok: Cy (7)
example.explanation: `validateUser` throws a `ValidationError` naming the bad field. Because the error is an instance of `ValidationError`, the catch prints its `name`, its `field`, and its `message`. Any other error would be rethrown. After each catch the loop moves on to the next line, so one bad record does not stop the rest.

practice.title: Bank withdrawals
practice.prompt:
Read a starting balance and one withdrawal per line, and print the result of each withdrawal.

1. Write `class InsufficientFundsError extends Error` whose constructor takes `needed` and `available`, calls `super` with the message `need <needed>, have <available>`, sets `this.name`, and stores both numbers.
2. Finish `withdraw(current, amount)`: throw an `InsufficientFundsError` when `amount` is more than `current`, otherwise return `current - amount`.
3. For each amount, update `balance` and print `Balance: <balance>`.
4. Catch only `InsufficientFundsError` (rethrow anything else), keep the balance unchanged, and print `<error name>: <message> (short <needed - available>)` using the error's fields.

Input:

```text
100
30
50
50
20
```

Expected output:

```text
Balance: 70
Balance: 20
InsufficientFundsError: need 50, have 20 (short 30)
Balance: 0
```

tests.output:
Balance: 70
Balance: 20
InsufficientFundsError: need 50, have 20 (short 30)
Balance: 0

hints: Build the message as a template literal from `needed` and `available`, and pass it to `super(...)` before setting `this.name`.
Assign `balance = withdraw(balance, amount);` inside try, so a throw leaves `balance` as it was.
Read the fields back in the catch: `error.needed - error.available`.

recap:
- `class Child extends Parent` inherits the parent's fields and methods.
- `super(...)` runs the parent constructor and must come before `this` in a child constructor.
- `super.method()` calls the parent version from inside an override.
- Same method name in a child overrides the parent. One loop calling it on mixed objects is polymorphism.
- A base method that throws `not implemented` forces subclasses to override it.
- `instanceof` checks the whole chain. A parse function with a `switch` picks the subclass.
- Methods live once on `ClassName.prototype`. `Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)` shows the link.
- `Object.hasOwn(obj, key)` checks own properties, `key in obj` checks the whole chain.
- Never add methods to built-in prototypes.
- `class MyError extends Error`: call `super(message)`, set `this.name`, add extra fields, catch with `instanceof`, and rethrow the rest.
